subject: Partner request: SDK deprecation window & versioning timeline coordination
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina@catalystworks.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: partnerships@catalystworks.com
Date: 2027-09-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SDK deprecation window + breaking change notice for upcoming API surface changes

Hi Rachel,

Quick note from CatalystWorks — we're seeing mentions in the partner changelog that Redwood plans to remove the legacy syncResponses endpoint and introduce a new streaming-first API in Q4. Our engineering and QA teams rely on the legacy SDK binding (v1.x) to power offline batch scoring and a connector shipped to multiple enterprise customers.

Can we get clarity on the exact deprecation timeline, and whether Redwood will provide a backwards-compatible adaptor or a defined compatibility window (e.g., 12 months from announcement)? If Redwood expects partners to move to the streaming API within 60 days, that will be disruptive for our customers and likely require co-ordinated release notes and regression testing.

We'd like to propose a partner sync next week to align on:
- Formal deprecation date and migration window
- Any SDK helper libraries/redwood-official adapters planned
- Testing artifacts Redwood can share (sample payloads, acceptance tests)

Attached: a short one-pager describing our expected impact (high-level).

Thanks — can you loop in whoever owns SDK lifecycle?

—Nina
Nina Patel
Director, Strategic Alliances | CatalystWorks
phone: +1 415 555 0199

Attachment: catalystworks-impact-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear note and the attached impact matrix. I appreciate you flagging customer impact early.

Short answer: we are planning a deprecation announcement for the legacy syncResponses endpoint, but we do not want to break partner integrations mid-cycle. I will pull together the proposed timeline and a draft of the partner compatibility commitments for review.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick 30-min sync on Tue 2027-09-07 at 10:00 PT (can you confirm?)
- I'll share our internal deprecation proposal and compatibility matrix ahead of that meeting (engineering + program owners cc'd).
- If needed, Redwood can provide a short-lived adaptor shim and an acceptance test harness.

Looping in Marissa (Partner AM) and Vanessa (Partner Partnerships) to coordinate docs and timelines.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim

Date: 2027-09-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: deprecation timeline + compatibility commitments (draft)

Hi all — attaching a draft deprecation plan and a simple compatibility matrix. High-level proposal:

- Announcement: 2027-09-15
- End of support (no SLA): 2028-03-15 (6 months of supported migration window)
- Removal (hard deprecation): 2028-09-15 (12 months from announcement)

We propose the following partner commitments from Redwood:
- Official migration guide and sample acceptance tests
- An adapter package (redwood-compat-adapter) maintained for 12 months post-announcement
- Weekly partner office hours for the first 8 weeks after announcement

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-deprecation-proposal.pdf, compatibility-matrix.csv

Marissa (Partner AM) — can you confirm the sales/contract implications so we can surface to legal if customers request SLA exceptions? Jonas, can you scan the compatibility matrix and flag any technical blockers (esp. for batch scoring use-cases)?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sdk-deprecation-proposal.pdf (PDF, 86KB); compatibility-matrix.csv (CSV, 8KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina@catalystworks.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: deprecation timeline + compatibility commitments (draft)

Thanks for the draft, Marissa. I reviewed the matrix and wanted to call out a few technical notes from infra/engine team perspective:

1) Streaming-first API is the recommended path for low-latency, long-context workloads. However, batch/offline scoring is a first-class scenario — we can support it with the new streaming surface via a short-lived server-side adapter.

2) Compatibility concerns: the biggest breaking change is the change in response framing and the removal of the legacy "full_response" envelope. We can provide a helper library that maps old payloads to the new streaming messages, but there will be subtle behavioral differences (e.g., tokenization/early-stopping heuristics) that require CAW vendor regression tests.

3) Implementation suggestion (low lift):
- Provide redwood-compat-adapter as a middleware that exposes the old syncResponses endpoint but proxies to the streaming infra. The adapter will buffer streaming events until completion and emit a single full_response for clients that expect that shape.
- Publish a reference implementation in our public partner repo with an MIT license.
- Provide an acceptance-test harness (python) which runs the same prompts against legacy and streaming paths and reports deltas.

I'll add a short developer note and expected ops cost estimate (approx 0.2 FTE for maintenance, plus a small SRE runbook) to the Drive doc. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cDriveLink

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
